memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in the sanctuary
area, because it is a most holy part of their perpetual share of the
food offerings presented to the LORD'" - Lev 24:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The bread that sat before God was not thrown away at the end of the
week. The priests ate it. What was offered to God became food for those
who served Him.

There is a quiet lesson here about God's provision. The priests owned no
farmland. Their living came from the offerings. God fed His servants
from His own table.

Dear friend, there is a striking moment in the Gospels connected to this
bread. When David was hungry and fleeing for his life, he ate the
consecrated bread that only priests were permitted to eat. Jesus
mentioned that story when the Pharisees criticised His hungry disciples
for picking grain on the Sabbath (Matt 12:3-4).

Jesus' point was not that God's laws do not matter. His point was that
God's laws were never meant to be used against the very people they were
given to serve. He said He desired mercy, not sacrifice.

Notice how the chapter's threads meet in Christ. He is the bread of life
(John 6:35), the true light (John 8:12), and the great High Priest who
feeds His people.

If you serve God today, He will also sustain you. Paul says my God will
meet all your needs according to the riches of His glory in Christ Jesus
(Phil 4:19).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trusting God to provide for me as I serve Him?
2. Do I ever use religious rules in a way that harms people?
3. Am I feeding on Christ, or only working for Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, You are the bread of life and You sustain those who serve
You. Feed my soul today, and make me merciful in how I treat others.
Amen.
